subject: Performance/SLO call — Private VPC qualification (recap & next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, elliot_price@redwood.com

Subject: Performance/SLO call — Private VPC qualification (recap & next steps)

Hi Ravi / Laura —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps to validate performance for a Private/VPC deployment: 

Key SLOs you called out:
- P95 end-to-end inference latency <= 200 ms for 2k-token requests (streaming enabled)
- Sustained throughput target: 100 requests/sec (average payload size ~800 tokens)
- Concurrent active connections target: 75 per region (burst to 150)
- Streaming chunk latency (per-chunk emission to client) <= 80 ms
- Cold-start budget: <= 500 ms for warm pool fallback; acceptable occasional warm-ups during scale events

Networking & deployment constraints we need to validate:
- Private VPC peering or Site-to-Site VPN between Acme and Redwood (we recommended peering for lower jitter)
- Egress rules: allow outbound TLS to our inference subnet and HTTPS endpoints (we'll provide IP ranges)
- Path MTU >= 1500 and no packet shaping on the app -> inference path
- Expected internal latency budget: app tier -> inference nodes <= 30 ms ideally, to keep p95 under 200 ms

Technical artifacts attached: redwood_acme_network_diagram.pdf (sample topology), iperf_results_20260709.csv (baseline from your infra we asked you to run pre-call)

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
1) Acme to share traceroute + mtr from two representative app hosts to the target subnet and re-run iperf (UDP + TCP) to the IPs in the diagram — Ravi to share by EOD Mon 7/13.
2) Redwood infra (Aditya + Eliot) to provide the exact IP ranges and ports (443, gRPC over 443) and a simple connectivity checklist for firewall/NAT.
3) We will run an agreed perf-test harness (simulated streaming requests) from one of your hosts to validate p95 and chunk latencies. Desired time window: Tue 7/14 morning PT.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive after initial tests to review results and finalize peering approach — target Wed 7/15 10:00 AM PT.

Please let me know if I missed anything. Ravi / Laura — if the SLOs above need to be adjusted, flag the specific numbers so we can run targeted tests.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 200 ms p95 target is for the full round-trip from our app service to Redwood and back, including any CDN/NAT hops. Internally we were hoping to budget <= 25-30 ms for the network hop.
- Concurrency: the 75 concurrent active connections is accurate for steady-state. We have scheduled load tests that will produce bursts to ~140 connections for short windows.

Action items on our side:
- We will re-run iperf from two app hosts (east-1 and west-1) against the target IPs and share logs by EOD Mon 7/13.
- I'll introduce our network engineer (cc'd: laura.chen) for the peering/VPN configuration calls.

A few questions for Aditya / Eliot:
1) Does Redwood support TCP keepalive and configurable idle timeouts on the inference connection? We want to ensure long-lived streaming sessions don't get dropped.
2) For peering, are you recommending AWS Transit Gateway peering, or is Site-to-Site VPN sufficient for initial validation?

Ravi

On Fri, Jul 10, 2026 at 3:05 PM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps to validate performance for a Private/VPC deployment:

Hey team — quick technical notes to clarify what we will test and what we will need from Acme: 

- Keepalives & idle timeouts: Redwood supports configurable TCP keepalive and application-level pings for streaming sessions. Default idle timeout is 10m; we can extend for long-lived sessions during tests.
- Preferred connectivity for production: VPC peering (or Transit Gateway) gives lower jitter than Site-to-Site VPN. For PoC it's fine to start with VPN (we used it for a few customers) — we will capture network jitter and recommend moving to peering if p95 is elevated.
- Ports: outbound 443 allowed; we also support mutual TLS for private deployments if you want stronger auth — we can provide certs or use your KMS.
- MTU: ensure PMTU discovery is allowed. Fragmentation increases latency under load.

Perf test plan (summary):
1) Baseline: iperf3 TCP & UDP (60s runs) from app hosts to our test endpoint — capture throughput, packet loss, jitter.
2) Traceroute/mtr (3 minute window) to capture per-hop latency variance.
3) Streaming simulation: replay of representative requests (payload distribution you provided) at 100 RPS sustained and bursts to 150 RPS for 2 minutes. Measure p50/p95/p99 end-to-end + chunk latency.
4) Gradual concurrency ramp: from 10 -> 75 -> 150 connections using client-side warm pools to measure cold-start behaviour.

I'll prepare the test harness and a simple checklist for firewall/NAT that Marissa can share. If you can share two host IPs and a contact for the network window, we'll schedule Tue morning.

- Aditya
